messages.speaker: X
messages.text: Also verify that negative results—no precipitate, reading unchanged—are explicitly written, since unlogged absences silently vanish and distort later review. A quick end-of-session scan for "did I record what *didn't* happen?" catches that gap before the notebook closes.

messages.speaker: Y
messages.text: A fixed two-word prompt at every observation slot—"nil" or "no change"—turns the absence check from a memory task into a reflex, so the end-of-session scan has almost nothing left to find. That tiny structural nudge is what keeps the practice from quietly lapsing on busy days.

messages.speaker: X
messages.text: That timestamp-gap audit is straightforward and catches the most common drift without needing any extra hardware. One caveat: if an instrument auto-stamps its own log, compare the notebook entry to the instrument log rather than to the wall clock.

messages.speaker: Y
messages.text: Agreed—always anchor the cross-check to the instrument's own stamped log, and note the device serial number in the notebook so the two records are unambiguously paired. A second simple safeguard is to transcribe the raw displayed value before adding any unit conversion or interpretation, keeping the verbatim datum intact.

messages.speaker: X
messages.text: Serial-number pairing removes ambiguity, and keeping the verbatim reading guards against accidental unit slip. If a correction is unavoidable, strike through the original line and write the fix beside it with your initials and date, so the audit trail survives.
